chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).

Regarding the man who dies while his wife is under his guardianship, but he has not yet consummated the marriage with her, he said: 'For her is half the dower, and for her is the inheritance complete.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance and dower share of a wife if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between death and divorce in Shia jurisprudence, affirming that the wife retains her full inheritance share because the marital bond was established by the contract (aqd) even without physical consummation. This ruling contrasts with the pre-Islamic practice and certain Sunni interpretations, emphasizing that the right to inheritance is not contingent upon sexual relations but rather the validity of the marriage contract itself. The hadith underscores the principle that the husband's death triggers the immediate vesting of inheritance rights, distinguishing it from the conditional nature of dower payment in cases of divorce.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)

regarding the man who died and under him was the wife, not having slept with her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For her is half the dower, and for her is the inheritance complete (her complete share, not half)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “About the case of a man who dies and has a wife with whom he has not gone to bed, one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam,
has said, ‘She must receive one-half of her mahr (dower) and complete inheritance.’”
